[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/BrooklynTech.jpg/250px-BrooklynTech.jpg)](/wiki/File:BrooklynTech.jpg)

Brooklyn Technical

Main article: [Brooklyn Technical High School](/wiki/Brooklyn_Technical_High_School "Brooklyn Technical High School")

One of the original three specialized high schools in New York City (the other two being Stuyvesant High School and Bronx High School of Science). In 1918, Dr. Albert L. Colston, chair of the Math Department at Manual Training High School, recommended establishing a technical high school for Brooklyn boys. His plan envisioned a heavy concentration of [math](/wiki/Math "Math"), science, and [drafting](/wiki/Technical_drawing "Technical drawing") courses with parallel paths leading either to college or to a technical career in industry. By 1922, Dr. Colston's concept was approved by the Board of Education, and Brooklyn Technical High School opened in a converted warehouse at 49 Flatbush Avenue Extension, with 2,400 students. This location, in the shadow of the [Manhattan Bridge](/wiki/Manhattan_Bridge "Manhattan Bridge"), is the reason the school seal bears the image of this bridge, rather than the [Brooklyn Bridge](/wiki/Brooklyn_Bridge "Brooklyn Bridge"). Brooklyn Tech would occupy one more location before settling into its current site, for which the groundbreaking was held in 1930.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Laguardia-school.jpg/250px-Laguardia-school.jpg)](/wiki/File:Laguardia-school.jpg)

LaGuardia in 2008

Main article: [Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School](/wiki/Fiorello_H._LaGuardia_High_School "Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School")

Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School is the only specialized high school in New York City that does not require that an applicant take the SHSAT. Rather, students are accepted through auditions in the fields of vocal music, instrumental music, visual arts, dance, drama, and technical theatre.

Within the US establishment, it was understood that ignoring the second offer and returning to the first put Khrushchev in a terrible position. Military preparations continued, and all active duty Air Force personnel were recalled to their bases for possible action. Robert Kennedy later recalled the mood: "We had not abandoned all hope, but what hope there was now rested with Khrushchev's revising his course within the next few hours. It was a hope, not an expectation. The expectation was military confrontation by Tuesday [30 October], and possibly tomorrow [29 October] ...."[[152]](#cite_note-:0-153)

At 8:05 pm EDT, the letter drafted earlier in the day was delivered. The message read, "As I read your letter, the key elements of your proposals—which seem generally acceptable as I understand them—are as follows: 1) You would agree to remove these weapons systems from Cuba under appropriate United Nations observation and supervision; and undertake, with suitable safe-guards, to halt the further introduction of such weapon systems into Cuba. 2) We, on our part, would agree—upon the establishment of adequate arrangements through the United Nations, to ensure the carrying out and continuation of these commitments (a) to remove promptly the quarantine measures now in effect and (b) to give assurances against the invasion of Cuba." The letter was also released directly to the press to ensure it could not be "delayed".[[153]](#cite_note-154) With the letter delivered, a deal was on the table. As Robert Kennedy noted, there was little expectation it would be accepted. At 9:00 pm EDT, the EXCOMM met again to review the actions for the following day. Plans were drawn up for air strikes on the missile sites as well as other economic targets, notably petroleum storage. McNamara stated that they had to "have two things ready: a government for Cuba, because we're going to need one; and secondly, plans for how to respond to the Soviet Union in Europe, because sure as hell they're going to do something there".[[154]](#cite_note-155)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Parthenon_restoration.gif/250px-Parthenon_restoration.gif)](/wiki/File:Parthenon_restoration.gif)

Animation showing the Parthenon in 2011 and how it looked originally

In the mid-5th century BC, when the Athenian Acropolis became the seat of the [Delian League](/wiki/Delian_League "Delian League"), [Pericles](/wiki/Pericles "Pericles") initiated the building project that lasted the entire second half of the century. The most important buildings visible on the Acropolis today – the Parthenon, the [Propylaia](/wiki/Propylaia_(Acropolis_of_Athens) "Propylaia (Acropolis of Athens)"), the [Erechtheion](/wiki/Erechtheion "Erechtheion") and the temple of [Athena Nike](/wiki/Athena_Nike "Athena Nike") – were erected during this period. The Parthenon was built under the general supervision of [Phidias](/wiki/Phidias "Phidias"), who also had charge of the sculptural decoration. The architects [Ictinos](/wiki/Ictinos "Ictinos") and [Callicrates](/wiki/Callicrates "Callicrates") began their work in 447, and the building was substantially completed by 432. Work on the decorations continued until at least 431.[[62]](#cite_note-62)

The Parthenon was built primarily by men who knew how to work marble. These quarrymen had exceptional skills and were able to cut the blocks of marble to very specific measurements. The quarrymen also knew how to avoid the faults, which were numerous in the [Pentelic marble](/wiki/Pentelic_marble "Pentelic marble"). If the marble blocks were not up to standard, the architects would reject them. The marble was worked with iron tools – picks, points, punches, chisels, and drills. The quarrymen would hold their tools against the marble block and firmly tap the surface of the rock.[[63]](#cite_note-auto-63)

A big project like the Parthenon attracted stonemasons from far and wide who travelled to Athens to assist in the project. Slaves and foreigners worked together with the Athenian citizens in the building of the Parthenon, doing the same jobs for the same pay. Temple building was a specialised craft, and there were not many men in Greece

There are many historical and contemporary claims of superlative height for species beyond those listed in the table above. For example, several articles published in 1878 describe an *[Eucalyptus amygdalina](/wiki/Eucalyptus_amygdalina "Eucalyptus amygdalina")* exceeding 380 feet (120 m) and others nearing 420 feet (130 m) up to 500 feet (150 m), including the [Nooksack Giant](/wiki/Nooksack_Giant "Nooksack Giant") which was measured using a tape at 465 feet (142 m) after being cut down.[[56]](#cite_note-57)[[57]](#cite_note-58)[[58]](#cite_note-59)

The heights of the tallest trees in the world have been the subject of considerable dispute and much exaggeration. Modern verified measurements with [laser rangefinders](/wiki/Laser_rangefinder "Laser rangefinder") or with [tape](/wiki/Measuring_tape "Measuring tape") drop measurements made by tree climbers (such as those carried out by canopy researchers), have shown that some older [tree height measurement](/wiki/Tree_height_measurement "Tree height measurement") methods are often unreliable, sometimes producing exaggerations of 5% to 15% or more above the real height.[[59]](#cite_note-60)

**AlphaGo** is a [computer program](/wiki/Computer_program "Computer program") that plays the [board game](/wiki/Board_game "Board game") [Go](/wiki/Go_(game) "Go (game)").[[1]](#cite_note-1) It was developed by the London-based [DeepMind](/wiki/DeepMind "DeepMind") Technologies,[[2]](#cite_note-2) an acquired subsidiary of [Google](/wiki/Google "Google"). Subsequent versions of AlphaGo became increasingly powerful, including a version that competed under the name [Master](/wiki/AlphaGo_Master "AlphaGo Master").[[3]](#cite_note-3) After retiring from competitive play, AlphaGo Master was succeeded by an even more powerful version known as [AlphaGo Zero](/wiki/AlphaGo_Zero "AlphaGo Zero"), which was completely [self-taught](/wiki/Self-play_(reinforcement_learning_technique) "Self-play (reinforcement learning technique)") without learning from human games. AlphaGo Zero was then generalized into a program known as [AlphaZero](/wiki/AlphaZero "AlphaZero"), which played additional games, including [chess](/wiki/Chess "Chess") and [shogi](/wiki/Shogi "Shogi"). AlphaZero has in turn been succeeded by a program known as [MuZero](/wiki/MuZero "MuZero") which learns without being taught the rules.

AlphaGo and its successors use a [Monte Carlo tree search](/wiki/Monte_Carlo_tree_search "Monte Carlo tree search") algorithm to find its moves based on knowledge previously acquired by [machine learning](/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), specifically by an [artificial neural network](/wiki/Artificial_neural_network "Artificial neural network") (a [deep learning](/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") method) by extensive training, both from human and computer play.[[4]](#cite_note-DeepMindnature2016-4) A neural network is trained to identify the best moves and the winning percentages of these moves. This neural network improves the strength of the tree search, resulting in stronger move selection in the next iteration.

They can discover and extract raw materials, [craft](/wiki/Glossary_of_video_game_terms#Crafting "Glossary of video game terms") tools and items, build structures, fight hostile [mobs](/wiki/Mob_(video_games) "Mob (video games)"), and cooperate with or compete against other players in [multiplayer](/wiki/Multiplayer "Multiplayer"). In addition, the game's large community offers a wide variety of [user-generated content](/wiki/User-generated_content "User-generated content"), such as [modifications](/wiki/Minecraft_modding "Minecraft modding"), [servers](/wiki/Minecraft_server "Minecraft server"), player [skins](/wiki/Video_game_skin "Video game skin"), [texture packs](/wiki/Texture_packs "Texture packs"), and custom maps, which add new game mechanics and possibilities.

Originally created by [Markus "Notch" Persson](/wiki/Markus_%22Notch%22_Persson "Markus \"Notch\" Persson") using the [Java](/wiki/Java_(programming_language) "Java (programming language)") programming language, [Jens "Jeb" Bergensten](/wiki/Jens_%22Jeb%22_Bergensten "Jens \"Jeb\" Bergensten") was handed control over the game's development following its full release. In November 2014, Mojang and the *Minecraft* intellectual property were purchased by [Microsoft](/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") for US$2.5 billion; [Xbox Game Studios](/wiki/Xbox_Game_Studios "Xbox Game Studios") hold the publishing rights for the *Bedrock Edition*, the unified [cross-platform](/wiki/Cross-platform_play "Cross-platform play") version which evolved from the *Pocket Edition* [codebase](/wiki/Codebase "Codebase")[[j]](#cite_note-13) and replaced the [legacy](/wiki/Legacy_software "Legacy software") console versions. *Bedrock* is updated concurrently with Mojang's original *Java Edition*, although with numerous, generally small, differences.

Main article: [Cervical screening](/wiki/Cervical_screening "Cervical screening")

Guidelines from the [American Cancer Society](/wiki/American_Cancer_Society "American Cancer Society") recommend different screening strategies for cervical cancer based on a woman's age, screening history, risk factors, and choice of tests.[[146]](#cite_note-146) Because of the link between HPV and cervical cancer, the ACS currently recommends early detection of cervical cancer in average-risk asymptomatic adults primarily with cervical cytology by Pap smear, regardless of HPV vaccination status. Women aged 30–65 should preferably be tested every 5 years with both the HPV test and the Pap test. In other age groups, a Pap test alone can suffice unless they have been diagnosed with [atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance](/wiki/Atypical_squamous_cells_of_undetermined_significance "Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance") (ASC-US).[[147]](#cite_note-147) Co-testing with a Pap test and HPV test is recommended because it decreases the rate of false-negatives. According to the National Cancer Institute, "The most common test detects DNA from several high-risk HPV types, but it cannot identify the types that are present. Another test is specific for DNA from HPV types 16 and 18, the two types that cause most HPV-associated cancers. A third test can detect DNA from several high-risk HPV types and can indicate whether HPV-16 or HPV-18 is present. A fourth test detects RNA from the most common high-risk HPV types. These tests can detect HPV infections before cell abnormalities are evident.

"Theoretically, the HPV DNA and RNA tests could be used to identify HPV infections in cells taken from any part of the body. However, the tests are approved by the FDA for only two indications: for follow-up testing of women who seem to have abnormal Pap test results and for cervical cancer screening in combination with a [Pap test](/wiki/Pap_test "Pap test") among women over age 30."[[148]](#cite_note-148)

During the 2021 off-season, the Devils signed free agent defenseman [Dougie Hamilton](/wiki/Dougie_Hamilton "Dougie Hamilton") from the Carolina Hurricanes.[[168]](#cite_note-169) General manager Tom Fitzgerald would also succeed in his goal to sign a backup goaltender and top 6 winger by signing veterans [Jonathan Bernier](/wiki/Jonathan_Bernier "Jonathan Bernier") and [Tomas Tatar](/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Tatar "Tomáš Tatar").[[169]](#cite_note-170)[[170]](#cite_note-171) However, the [2021–22 season](/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NHL_season "2021–22 NHL season") fared to be no better as the Devils once again missed the playoffs. At the end of the season, Nasreddine was not tendered a contract extension, and [Mark Recchi](/wiki/Mark_Recchi "Mark Recchi") was fired from his assistant coach position.[[171]](#cite_note-172)

In the [2022–23 season](/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NHL_season "2022–23 NHL season"), the team rebounded by recording its best regular season in franchise history. Spurred on by a franchise-record 13-game winning streak in October and November, the Devils finished third in the entire league and set a franchise record for wins (52) and points (112). The team's climb from 63 points the prior season to 112 points marked the largest single-season increase by any NHL team in an 82-game season. In addition to a breakout season from newly acquired goaltender [Vitek Vanecek](/wiki/V%C3%ADtek_Van%C4%9B%C4%8Dek "Vítek Vaněček"), the Devils were led by impressive offensive performances from Hughes, Hischier, Hamilton, and [Jesper Bratt](/wiki/Jesper_Bratt "Jesper Bratt"). All four players eclipsed the 70-point mark, while Hughes set a franchise record for most points in a single season by a Devils player with 99 points. Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald built further on this impressive offensive core by acquiring All-Star forward [Timo Meier](/wiki/Timo_Meier "Timo Meier") in a mid-season trade from the [San Jose Sharks](/wiki/San_Jose_Sharks "San Jose Sharks"). Main article: [Geography of Denmark](/wiki/Geography_of_Denmark "Geography of Denmark")

See also: [Geography of the Faroe Islands](/wiki/Geography_of_the_Faroe_Islands "Geography of the Faroe Islands") and [Geography of Greenland](/wiki/Geography_of_Greenland "Geography of Greenland")

[![Satellite image](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Satellite_image_of_Denmark_in_July_2001.jpg/250px-Satellite_image_of_Denmark_in_July_2001.jpg)](/wiki/File:Satellite_image_of_Denmark_in_July_2001.jpg)

A satellite image of Jutland and the Danish islands

Located in [Northern Europe](/wiki/Northern_Europe "Northern Europe"), Denmark[[N 6]](#cite_note-proper-21) consists of the northern part of the [Jutland](/wiki/Jutland "Jutland") peninsula and an [archipelago](/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of [406 islands](/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Denmark "List of islands of Denmark").[[15]](#cite_note-islands-23) Of these, the largest island is [Zealand](/wiki/Zealand "Zealand"), on which the capital [Copenhagen](/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen") is situated, followed by the [North Jutlandic Island](/wiki/North_Jutlandic_Island "North Jutlandic Island"), [Funen](/wiki/Funen "Funen"), and [Lolland](/wiki/Lolland "Lolland").[[63]](#cite_note-72) The island of [Bornholm](/wiki/Bornholm "Bornholm") is located some 150 km east of the rest of the country, in the [Baltic Sea](/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea"). Many of the larger islands are connected by bridges; a [bridge-tunnel](/wiki/%C3%98resund_Bridge "Øresund Bridge") across the [Øresund](/wiki/%C3%98resund "Øresund") connects Zealand with Sweden; the [Great Belt Fixed Link](/wiki/Great_Belt_Fixed_Link "Great Belt Fixed Link") connects Funen with Zealand; and the [Little Belt Bridge](/wiki/Little_Belt_Bridge_(1970) "Little Belt Bridge (1970)") connects Jutland with Funen. [Ferries](/wiki/Ferry "Ferry") or [small aircraft](/wiki/Small_aircraft "Small aircraft") connect to the smaller islands. English is a [pluricentric language](/wiki/Pluricentric_language "Pluricentric language"), which means that no one national authority sets the standard for use of the language.[[93]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETrudgillHannah20082-93)[[94]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERomaine1999-94)[[95]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaughCable2002-95)[[96]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETrudgillHannah20088–9-96) Spoken English, including English used in broadcasting, generally follows national pronunciation standards that are established by custom rather than by regulation. International broadcasters are usually identifiable as coming from one country rather than another through their [accents](/wiki/Accent_(sociolinguistics) "Accent (sociolinguistics)"),[[97]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETrudgill2006-97) but newsreader scripts are also composed largely in international [standard written English](/wiki/Standard_written_English "Standard written English"). The norms of standard written English are maintained purely by the consensus of educated English speakers around the world, without any oversight by any government or international organisation.[[98]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmmon20081537–1539-98)

American listeners readily understand most British broadcasting, and British listeners readily understand most American broadcasting. Most English speakers around the world can understand radio programmes, television programmes, and films from many parts of the [English-speaking world](/wiki/English-speaking_world "English-speaking world").[[99]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESvartvikLeech2006122-99) Both standard and non-standard varieties of English can include both formal or informal styles, distinguished by word choice and syntax and use both technical and non-technical registers.[[100]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETrudgillHannah20085–6-100)

The settlement history of the English-speaking inner circle countries outside Britain helped level dialect distinctions and produce [koiné](/wiki/Koin%C3%A9 "Koiné") forms of English in South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand.[[101]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDeumert2006130-101) The majority of immigrants to the United States without

Since the series' last episode premiering in 2017, the show's impact and Lena Dunham's identity have inevitably evolved.[[103]](#cite_note-103) Initially hyped and criticized for various reasons, including lack of diversity, *Girls* became a cultural lightning rod. Over the years, Dunham distanced herself from the show, focusing on personal and professional growth. The show's satirical elements and its influence on the portrayal of sex and body image with disarming honesty trademark its originality. Despite initial controversy, *Girls* is appreciated for this originality and its contribution to feminist television.[[104]](#cite_note-104)[[105]](#cite_note-105)

In December 2023, *Variety* ranked *Girls* #86 on its list of the 100 greatest TV shows of all time.[[106]](#cite_note-106)

Besides sightseeing from the highway, Big Sur offers hiking and outdoor activities.
